English Literature.question: ১) The literary work 'Pygmalion' was written by Nobel Prize winner-
English Literature.exp:
George Bernard Shaw (1856-1950):
Irish comic dramatist, literary critic, and socialist propagandist, winner of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1925.
Famous Plays of G.B. Shaw are-
Pygmalion
Mrs. Warren’s Profession
Arms and the Man
Heartbreak House
Caesar and Cleopatra
Man and Superman
The Doctor’s Dilemma
St. Joan of Arc
[Source: An ABC of English Literature - Dr M Mofizar Rahman and Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২) Which one is the autobiographical book written by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam?
English Literature.exp:
A.P.J. Abdul Kalam was the 11th president of India.
His famous books:
Wings of Fire(an autobiography, 1999), Ignited Mind, Inspiring Thought, The Luminous Sparks, Turning Points, You are Born to Bloom, Target 3 Billion, Indomitable Spirit, My Journey etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩) Who is the author of the novel 'Brave New World'?
English Literature.exp:
Aldous Huxley(1894–1963), English novelist and critic. He remains best known for one novel, ‘Brave New World (1932)’, a model for much dystopian science fiction that followed.
His other notable works: Eyeless in Gaza, After Many a Summer Dies the Swan, Point Counter Point, Crome Yellow, Antic Hay, The Doors of Perception, Those Barren Leaves, The Devils of Loudun etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪) Alice Munro is a Canadian-
English Literature.exp:
Alice Munro:
Canadian short-story writer who gained international recognition with her exquisitely drawn narratives.
-The Swedish Academy dubbed her a “master of the contemporary short story” when it awarded her the Nobel Prize for Literature in 2013.
Her notable works: Runaway, Dance of the Happy Shades, The Lives of Girls and Women, The Bear Came over the Mountain, The View from Castle Rock, Dear Life, etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৫) Who wrote the book ‘The Luminous Sparks’?
English Literature.exp:
The Luminous Sparks:
A Biography In Verse And Colours Written By Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Other notable works of A.P.J. Abdul Kalam: Wings of Fire, Ignited Mind, Inspiring Thought, Turning Points, You are Born to Bloom, Target 3 Billion, Indomitable Spirit, My Journey etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৬) Whose famous work is 'Death of a Salesman'?
English Literature.exp:
Arthur Miller:
American playwright Arthur Miller is known for combining social awareness with a searching concern for his characters’ inner lives.
He is best known for ‘Death of a Salesman (1949)’.
His other notable works: After the Fall, All My Sons, The Crucible, The Price, The American Clock, Incident at Vichy.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৭) Who wrote the preamble of Rabindranath Tagore’s ''Song Offerings''?
English Literature.exp:
William Butler Yeats (1865 – 1939):
- Irish dramatist, poet and critic.
- He is famous for his use of “Symbolism and Mysticism”.
- He wrote the preamble of Tagore's ''Song Offerings'' in 1912, which later got nobel prize in 1913.
- W.B Yeats got the Nobel prize in 1923.
Major Works:
Poems: The wild swans at coole, The Tower, The Winding Stair and Other poems, The Resurrection, The Second Coming, The Cat and the Moon, Byzantium, The Lake Isle of Innisfree, Among School Children, The Lord of Harts, falling of leaves, A prayer for My Daughter, When You Are Old.
Drama: The countess Cathleen, Cathleen in Houlihan.
[Source: Brittanica.com and Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৮) ‘The Ministry of Utmost Happiness’ is written by-
English Literature.exp:
Arundhati Roy, Indian author, actress, and political activist who was best known for the award-winning novel ‘The God of Small Things (1997)’ and for her involvement in environmental and human rights causes.
Among her publications were Power Politics (2001), The Algebra of Infinite Justice (2002), War Talk (2003), Public Power in the Age of Empire (2004), Field Notes on Democracy: Listening to Grasshoppers (2009), Broken Republic: Three Essays (2011), and Capitalism: A Ghost Story (2014).
In 2017 Roy published ‘The Ministry of Utmost Happiness’.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৯) Who is often called the 'Father of Modern African Literature'?
English Literature.exp:
Chinua Achebe(1930-2013):
-One of the world's most widely recognized and praised Nigerian novelists.
-Chinua Achebe wrote some of the most extraordinary works of the 20th century.
Things Fall Apart (1958), Achebe’s first novel, concerns traditional Igbo life at the time of the advent of missionaries and colonial government in his homeland.
His other Notable works: No Longer at Ease, Arrow of God, A Man of the People, Anthills of the Savannah.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১০) Who is the author of ‘The Conquest of Happiness’?
English Literature.exp:
Bertrand Arthur William Russell(1872–1970):
-British philosopher, logician, and social reformer, founding figure in the analytic movement in Anglo-American philosophy, and recipient of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1950.
His notable works: Principia Mathematica, Mysticism and Logic and Other Essays, Why I Am Not a Christian, The Problems of Philosophy (1911), The Analysis of Mind (1921), The Analysis of Matter (1927), On Education (1926), Marriage and Morals (1929), The Conquest of Happiness (1930), A History of Western Philosophy (1945), Human Knowledge: Its Scope and Limits (1948), etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১১) Which of the following is a semi-autobiographical novel by D.H. Lawrence?
English Literature.exp:
D.H. Lawrence(1885-1930):
In full David Herbert Lawrence.
-English author of novels, short stories, poems, plays, essays, travel books, and letters.
-His novels Sons and Lovers (1913, Semi-autobiographical), The Rainbow (1915), and Women in Love (1920) made him one of the most influential English writers of the 20th century.
His other novels: The White Peacock, Lady Chatterley's Lover, Aaron’s Rod, Kangaroo etc.
His famous short stories: The Virgin and the Gypsy, The Rocking Horse Winner, The Captain Doll, The Labybird, The Price, The Fox.
His plays: Touch and Go, The Married Man.His Poems: The White Horse, Birds Beasts and Flowers.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১২) ‘The Raven’ is a famous poem written by-
English Literature.exp:
Edgar Allan Poe(1809–49):
American short-story writer, poet, critic, and editor who is famous for his cultivation of mystery and the macabre.
His tale ''The Murders in the Rue Morgue'' (1841) initiated the modern detective story, and the atmosphere in his tales of horror is unrivaled in American fiction.
His some other notable works are:
- The Black Cat
- The Tell-Tale Heart
- The Masque of the Red Death
- The Murders in the Rue Morgue
- The Fall of the House of Usher etc.
His ''The Raven'' (1845) numbers among the best-known poems in the national literature.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৩) Who is the author of the novel ‘Howards End’?
English Literature.exp:
E.M. Forster(1879-1970):
In full Edward Morgan Forster.
British novelist, essayist, and social and literary critic.
His fame rests largely on his novels Howards End (1910) and A Passage to India (1924) and on a large body of criticism.
Foster's other works:
- A Passage to India
- Aspects of Novel
- Where Angels Fear to Tread
- The Longest Journey
- A Room With a View
- The Celestial Omnibus(Collection of short stories).
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৪) Ernest Hemingway is a/an -
English Literature.exp:
Ernest Hemingway(1899-1961) is an American novelist and short-story writer.
He was awarded the Nobel prize in 1954 for literature.
His famous novels are- For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Old Man and The Sea, A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises, Death in the Afternoon, To Have and Have not.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture].

English Literature.question: ১৫) Who wrote ‘The Cantos’?
English Literature.exp:
The Cantos, collection of poems by Ezra Pound(American poet and critic), who began writing these more or less philosophical reveries in 1915.
- The first were published in Poetry magazine in 1917; through the decades, the writing of cantos gradually became Pound’s major poetic occupation, and the last were published in 1968.
-The complete edition of The Cantos (1970) consists of 117 sections.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৬) Who was one of the best-known Latin American writers?
English Literature.exp:
Gabriel García Márquez(1927-2014):
-He was one of the best-known Latin American writers in history.
-He won a Nobel Prize for Literature, mostly for his masterpiece of magic realism, Cien años de soledad (1967; One Hundred Years of Solitude).
His other notable works: Love in the Time of Cholera, No One Writes to the Colonel, News of a Kidnapping, Memories of My Melancholy Whores, The Leaf Storm.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৭) George Orwell's novel ‘Nineteen Eighty Four’ was published in-
English Literature.exp:
Nineteen Eighty-four, novel by English author George Orwell (pseudonym of Eric Arthur Blair) published in 1949 as a warning against totalitarianism. His other famous novel is ‘Animal Farm (1945)’.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৮) ‘The Power and the Glory’ a famous work of-
English Literature.exp:
Graham Greene(2 October 1904 – 3 April 1991):
-In full Henry Graham Greene.
-English novelist, short-story writer, playwright, and journalist whose novels treat life’s moral ambiguities in the context of contemporary political settings.
His notable works: Brighton Rock, The Power and the Glory (1940), The End of the Affair, A Burnt-Out Case, The Comedians, Our Man in Havana, The Quiet American, The Human Factor, Stamboul Train.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ১৯) Which of these is a science fiction novel by English author H.G. Wells?
English Literature.option3: গ) The War of the Worlds
English Literature.option4: ঘ) The History of Mr. Polly
English Literature.exp:
H.G. Wells(1866-1946):
-In full Herbert George Wells.
-English novelist, journalist, sociologist, and historian best known for such science fiction novels as The Time Machine and The War of the Worlds and such comic novels as Tono-Bungay and The History of Mr. Polly.
His other science fiction novels: The Wonderful Visit (1895), The Island of Doctor Moreau (1896), The Invisible Man (1897), The First Men in the Moon (1901), and The Food of the Gods (1904).
He also wrote many short stories, which were collected in The Stolen Bacillus (1895), The Plattner Story (1897), and Tales of Space and Time (1899).
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২০) Who is the author of the drama 'The Birthday Party'?
English Literature.exp:
The Birthday Party, drama in three acts by Harold Pinter (British dramatist), produced in 1958 and published in 1959.
His other notable works: The Dumb Waiter, The Caretaker, The Homecoming, The Room.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২১) Who has written the short story “Heart of Darkness”?
English Literature.exp:
Joseph Conrad(1857-1924):
English novelist and short-story writer of Polish descent, whose works include the novels Lord Jim (1900), Nostromo (1904), and The Secret Agent (1907) and the short story “Heart of Darkness” (1902).
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২২) ‘The Wings of the Dove’ is a novel written by -
English Literature.exp:
The Wings of the Dove, novel by Henry James, published in 1902.
-It explores one of James’s favourite themes: the cultural clash between naive Americans and sophisticated, often decadent Europeans.
Jame's other novels: Daisy Miller (1879), The Portrait of a Lady (1881), The Bostonians (1886), The Ambassadors (1903), Washington Square etc.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৩) Who is the creator of the popular and critically acclaimed ‘Harry Potter’ series?
English Literature.exp:
J.K. Rowling, in full Joanne Kathleen Rowling, (born July 31, 1965, Yate, near Bristol, England), British author, creator of the popular and critically acclaimed Harry Potter series, about a young sorcerer in training.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৪) Which one is a three-act play by John Millington Synge?
English Literature.option3: গ) A Memory of Two Mondays
English Literature.option4: ঘ) The Playboy of the Western World
English Literature.exp:
J.M. Synge(1871-1909):
In full John Millington Synge, leading figure in the Irish literary renaissance. The Playboy of the Western World, comedy in three acts by J.M. Synge, published and produced in 1907.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৫) Who is famous for introducing the narrative technique ‘Stream of consciousness’?
English Literature.exp:
James Joyce is famous for his narrative technique known as Stream of Consciousness.
His famous works are Exiles, Ulysses, A Portrait of the Artist as a Young Man.
[Source: Live MCQ lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৬) ‘Ulysses’ is a novel written by ___ James Joyce.
English Literature.exp:
Ulysses, novel by Irish writer James Joyce, first published in book form in 1922.
The novel is constructed as a modern parallel to Homer’s Odyssey.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৭) Who among the following voluntarily refused the Nobel Prize?
English Literature.exp:
Jean-Paul Sartre(1905–1980):
-He was a French novelist, playwright, and philosopher.
-A leading figure in 20th-century French philosophy, he was an exponent of a philosophy of existence known as existentialism.
His most notable works included Nausea (1938), Being and Nothingness (1943), and Existentialism and Humanism (1946).He was awarded the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1964, but he declined it.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৮) ‘Salt-Water Ballads’ is a literary work by-
English Literature.exp:
John Masefield(1878-1967):
-He is a British poet.
-Best known for his poems of the sea, ‘Salt-Water Ballads’ (1902, including “Sea Fever” and “Cargoes”), and for his long narrative poems, such as ‘The Everlasting Mercy’ (1911).
His other notable works: Dauber, Reynard the Fox.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ২৯) ‘Around the World in Eighty Days’ is a adventure novel written by-
English Literature.exp:
Around the World in Eighty Days, travel adventure novel by French author Jules Verne, published serially in 1872 in Le Temps and in book form in 1873.
His notable works: A Journey to the Centre of the Earth, The Mysterious Island, Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea, From the Earth to the Moon, Five Weeks in a Balloon.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩০) Who wrote the historical novel ‘War and Peace’?
English Literature.exp:
Leo Tolstoy(1828-1910):
Russian author Leo Tolstoy is considered a master of realistic fiction and one of the world’s greatest novelists, especially known for his two longest works, War and Peace (1865–69) and Anna Karenina (1875–77), which are commonly regarded as among the finest novels ever written..
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩১) Who wrote the novel ‘Mother’?
English Literature.exp:
Maxim Gorky(1868-1936):
Russian-Soviet writer who wrote stories, novels, and plays.
His notable works: Mother, My Childhood, In the World, The Lower Depths etc.
[Source:Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩২) In which short story are the characters of a young couple named Jim and Della?
English Literature.option2: খ) The Ransom of Red Chief
English Literature.option3: গ) The Gift of the Magi
English Literature.exp:
The Gift of the Magi, short story by American writer O. Henry (William Sidney Porter), published in the New York Sunday World in 1905 and then collected in The Four Million (1906).
The story concerns James(Jim) and Della Dillingham Young, a young couple who, despite their poverty, individually resolve to give each other an elegant gift on Christmas Eve.
[Source:Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৩) Who was the first American woman to win the Nobel prize for literature?
English Literature.exp:
Pearl S. Buck(1892 - 1973):
-She is an American novelist and writer.
-She was awarded the Nobel prize in 1938 for her rich and truly epic description of peasant life in China.
-Pearl S. Buck was the first American woman to win the Nobel prize for literature.
Works: The good earth, Pavilion of women, Imperial women, A House Divided.
[Source: Live MCQ lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৩৪) ‘Mending Wall’ is a poem by-
English Literature.exp:
Robert Frost(1874-1963): He is an American poet.
His famous poems: Road not Taken, Mending Wall, Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening, Christmas Trees, A Boy’s Will, North of Boston, Nothing Gold Can Stay, After Apple-picking, Home Burial, A Way Out.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৫) Who is the creator of the ‘Mowgli’ fictional character?
English Literature.exp:
Rudyard Kipling(1865-1936):
He is the first British to win a Nobel prize in 1907. He is mainly a Short Story writer.
His famous works are- Kim, The Jungle Book (Short Story), Plain Tales from The Hills, The Tomb of His Ancestors, The Man who was, The Mark of the Beast etc.
Mowgli, fictional character, an Indian boy raised by wolves who is the central figure in The Jungle Book (1894) and its sequel (1895).
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৬) Who wrote the absurd play 'Waiting for Godot'?
English Literature.exp:
Samuel Becket(1906-1989):
He is an Irish novelist, author, critic, and playwright, winner of the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1969. He wrote in both French and English and is perhaps best known for his plays, especially Waiting for Godot(Absurd play).
His Other notable works: The Unnamable, Molloy, Watt, Endgame, Malone Dies, Murphy, Krapp’s Last Tape, Dream of Fair to Middling Women, Whoroscope etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৩৭) ‘Les Miserable’ is a famous French novel by-
English Literature.exp:
Victor Hugo(1802-1885): He is a French Poet, Novelist and Dramatist.
His famous Novels are Les Miserable, Ninety-Three, The Hunchback of Notre Dame (First Novel), The Man Who Laughs. Autumn Leaves, Songs of the Twilight, Inner Voice, Rays and Shadows his famous poems.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৮) Among the following, who is famous for 'Presentation of inner realities'?
English Literature.exp:
Virginia woolf(1882–1941):
She was a British female novelist. She is famous for ‘Presentation of inner realities’.
Her famous novels are: The Voyage Out (first novel), To the Lighthouse, Mrs. Dalloway, Orlando: A biography etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৩৯) ‘The Sound and the Fury’ and ‘As I Lay Dying’ written by-
English Literature.exp:
William Faulkner(1897-1962):
-American novelist and short-story writer who was awarded the 1949 Nobel Prize for Literature.
-He is best remembered for his novels ‘The Sound and the Fury (1929)’, ‘As I Lay Dying (1930)’, ‘Sanctuary (1931)’, and ‘Absalom, Absalom! (1936)’ etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৪০) William Gerald Golding awarded Nobel Prize in 1983 for his novel -
English Literature.exp:
William Gerald Golding(1911-1993):
-British novelist, dramatist and poet.
-Awarded Nobel Prize in 1983 for his novel ‘Lord of the Files’.
His other Notable works: Darkness Visible,The Pyramid, Pincher Martin, Free Fall, The Inheritors, The Spire etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪১) The literary work ‘The Land of Promise' is-
English Literature.option1: ক) A novel by D.H. Lawrence
English Literature.option2: খ) A short story by Samuel Beckett
English Literature.option3: গ) A play by W. Somerset Maugham
English Literature.option4: ঘ) A poem by T.S. Eliot
English Literature.exp:
William Somerset Maugham(1874 – 1965):
He is a novelist playwright and story writer. He wrote the play 'The Land of Promise'.
His famous Novels are- Of Human Bondage, The Sacred Flames, The Razor's Edge, Cakes and Ale, The Musician, The Moon and Sixpence, Lady Frederick.
Short Stories: The Ant and the Grasshopper, the Luncheon.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৪২) ‘Good fences make good neighbors.’-who wrote this?
English Literature.exp:
‘Good fences make good neighbors.’ is from Mending Wall by Robert Frost.
He is an American Poet. His notable works: The Road Not Taken, The Death of the Hired Man, Mending Wall, Mountain Interval, Storm Fear, New Hampshire, North of Boston.
[Source: poets.org and Live MCQ Lecture.]

English Literature.question: ৪৩) 'An honest man is the noblest work of God' was stated by-
English Literature.exp:
Alexander Pope is a Mock Heroic Poet.
His famous quotation are-
-'Fools rush in where angels fear to tread'
-'An honest man is the noblest work of God'
-'To err is human, nto forgive is divine'
-'A little learning is a dangerous thing'.
[Source: An Essay on Criticism by Alexander Pope, Live MCQ Lecture]

English Literature.question: ৪৪) Alexandre Dumas was a famous-
English Literature.exp:
Alexandre Dumas one of the most prolific and most popular French authors of the 19th century. Without ever attaining indisputable literary merit, Dumas succeeded in gaining a great reputation first as a dramatist and then as a historical novelist, especially for such works as ‘The Count of Monte Cristo’ and ‘The Three Musketeers’.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৫) ‘Dream is not that which you see while sleeping; It is something that will not let you sleep’ was stated by-
English Literature.exp:
‘Dream is not that which you see while sleeping; It is something that will not let you sleep’ quotes by Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.He was an Indian scientist and politician who played a leading role in the development of India’s missile and nuclear weapons programs. He was president of India from 2002 to 2007.
[Source: Wings of Fire Book, written by A.P.J. Abdul Kalam]

English Literature.question: ৪৬) Which one was the first novel of Chinua Achebe?
English Literature.exp:
Chinua Achebe(1930-2013):
One of the world's most widely recognized and praised Nigerian novelists.
-Chinua Achebe wrote some of the most extraordinary works of the 20th century.
Things Fall Apart (1958), Achebe’s first novel, concerns traditional Igbo life at the time of the advent of missionaries and colonial government in his homeland.
His other Notable works: No Longer at Ease, Arrow of God, A Man of the People, Anthills of the Savannah.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৭) ‘The White Peacock’ is a novel written by-
English Literature.exp:
D.H. Lawrence(1885-1930):
In full David Herbert Lawrence.
-English author of novels, short stories, poems, plays, essays, travel books, and letters.
-His novels Sons and Lovers (1913), The Rainbow (1915), and Women in Love (1920) made him one of the most influential English writers of the 20th century.
His other novels: The White Peacock, Lady Chatterley's Lover, Aaron’s Rod, Kangaroo etc.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৮) Which of the following novels was written by Ernest Hemingway?
English Literature.option3: গ) A Room with a View
English Literature.option4: ঘ) To Have and Have not
English Literature.exp:
Ernest Hemingway(1899-1961): He is an American novelist and short-story writer.
To Have and Have Not, minor novel by Ernest Hemingway, published in 1937.
His other famous novels are- For Whom The Bell Tolls, The Old Man and The Sea, A Farewell to Arms, The Sun Also Rises, Death in the Afternoon.
In 1925 his first important book, a collection of stories called In Our Time, was published in New York City; it was originally released in Paris in 1924.
[Source: Live MCQ Lecture and Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৪৯) ‘Love in the Time of Cholera’ is a novel written by-
English Literature.exp:
Gabriel García Márquez(1927-2014):
-He was one of the best-known Latin American writers in history.
-Love in the Time of Cholera, novel by Gabriel Garcia Marquez, published in 1985 as El amor en los tiempos del cólera. The story, which treats the themes of love, aging, and death, takes place between the late 1870s and the early 1930s in a South American community troubled by wars and outbreaks of cholera.
-It is a tale of two lovers, artistic Florentino Ariza and wealthy Fermina Daza, who reunite after a lifetime apart.
[Source: Encyclopaedia Britannica]

English Literature.question: ৫০) ‘We are only strong as we are united as weak as we are divided’ is a quote by-
English Literature.exp:
‘We are only strong as we are united as weak as we are divided’ is a quote by J.K. Rowling.
She is a British author, creator of the popular and critically acclaimed Harry Potter series.[ Verified Source: https://www.researchgate.net/]
